user.title: Set up a Teltonika NTP server
user.description: Enter the address and WebUI credentials of your Teltonika NTP server (for example the NTP001).

data_description.host: IP address or host name. HTTPS is used; type http:// in front only if the device has no HTTPS (the password is then sent unencrypted).
data_description.username: A WebUI user. A dedicated read-only user for Home Assistant is recommended.
data_description.verify_ssl: Leave off for the device's default self-signed certificate: it is then pinned on the first connection, and a different certificate is refused afterwards.

dhcp_confirm.title: Teltonika NTP server discovered
dhcp_confirm.description: {name} was found at {host}. Enter its WebUI credentials to add it.

data_description.username: A WebUI user. A dedicated read-only user for Home Assistant is recommended.

reauth_confirm.title: Log in to {name} again
reauth_confirm.description: The device at {host} rejected the stored credentials.

data_description.username: A WebUI user. A dedicated read-only user for Home Assistant is recommended.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Teltonika NTP server

data_description.host: IP address or host name. HTTPS is used; type http:// in front only if the device has no HTTPS (the password is then sent unencrypted).
data_description.username: A WebUI user. A dedicated read-only user for Home Assistant is recommended.
data_description.verify_ssl: Leave off for the device's default self-signed certificate: it is then pinned on the first connection, and a different certificate is refused afterwards.

reconfigure.description: Change the address or credentials. This also accepts the certificate the device presents now, for example after a firmware reset replaced it.

error.invalid_host: Enter a host name or IP address, optionally with a port, without a path.

abort.not_supported: This Teltonika device is not an NTP server. Use the built-in Teltonika integration for routers.
abort.wrong_device: These details belong to a different device.

certificate_mismatch.title: Certificate of {name} changed
certificate_mismatch.description:
The Teltonika NTP server {name} presented another TLS certificate than the one Home Assistant pinned, so Home Assistant stopped sending it the password.

This happens after a firmware reset or a certificate renewal on the device, but can also mean that another device is posing as your NTP server.

If you replaced the certificate yourself, open the integration, choose **Reconfigure** and enter the credentials again to accept the new certificate.

insecure_http.title: {name} uses unencrypted HTTP
insecure_http.description:
The connection to {name} is set up with an http:// address, so the WebUI password travels unencrypted over the network.

Enable HTTPS on the device, then open the integration, choose **Reconfigure** and enter the address without http://.
